title: Final review of the Phase 2 diff
description: Review the full Phase 2 diff against the epic acceptance and SPEC §12 Phase 2, with the two operator constraints as the checklist: (a) is orchestration config and logic TRULY extracted from ticks — no execution package left behind, no unpinned read of a ticks-owned file, no ticks Go import; and (b) is the herdr executor robust to a herdr upgrade — a supported range rather than a point, capabilities read, required fields loud, the wire vocabulary pinned and diffed against the server's schema, no verdict derived from the substrate. Resolve or route findings before close-out. Verify a claimed defect against the base commit BEFORE any repair is built on it: the Phase 1 epic lost a wave to a repair built on a defect that did not exist.
notes: 2026-09-14 08:27 - Defect pass (opus, read-only) on the Phase 2 diff: 2 blockers, 7 should-fix, 5 nits. Both blockers violate the epic's OWN x6j guarantee inside the code that claims it — a launch slower than the client call timeout becomes a verdict AND tears down a live agent (verified: DefaultStartupTimeout 60s vs DefaultCallTimeout 30s), and Cancel writes a cancellation over an attempt that already reported, renaming a succeeded verdict. Routed as ticks 1eq (blockers) and etp (the seven should-fix, all the same family: an unknown answered as a fact). CRITICAL CONTEXT, verified in code: usableProfile (internal/reconcile/profiles.go:307) refuses any profile whose executor is not local-subprocess, so nothing constructs herdr.Executor outside tests. Every finding is LATENT — they are what a first real run would hit. Two guarantees confirmed genuinely held: the executor seam (the no-herdr-code check is enforced, not asserted) and durable-evidence-only collect (no client call in that path; the all-errors fixture really drives a verdict from the report alone).
